description: Versioned required native acceptance checks per chunk. xtask requires a native-acceptance record to report exactly this ID set, each with result pass, a nonempty observation and at least one evidence file listed in the review packet. Changing a list is a reviewed source change.

C01.check: Fixture app launches from the prepared bundle; window title 'Prisma AIRS Desktop v2 (Fixture)'; rail shows 'Fixture build'.
Native menus: app menu (About, Settings… Cmd+,, Hide, Quit), Edit, View (Command Palette… Cmd+K, Appearance, zoom), Go (destinations Cmd+1–Cmd+9), Window.

Keyboard only: Tab reaches the Features navigation; Enter on a destination moves focus to its heading and marks it current; a visible focus ring is rendered on focused controls (fixture WebView self-capture).
Cmd+K opens the palette with focus in the field; typing filters; Enter navigates and closes; Escape closes and restores focus to the previously focused control.
Go-menu shortcuts (Cmd+2 Academy, Cmd+, Settings) navigate through the native menu and observation channel, including while the palette is open (palette closes, heading receives focus).

Every product destination not yet implemented states it is not available in this build with its planned chunk and shows no data or service contact; Runtime Security (available since C03) opens its scan view instead.
Settings > Appearance and View > Appearance change the general theme (Paper light / Gruvbox dark / match system) only after the native snapshot arrives.

Accessibility tree: 'Features' navigation landmark; destination buttons expose names (unavailable ones including 'Not available in this build'); the current destination is exposed; page headings are in reading order. Records which AX attributes were inspected; spoken VoiceOver output is not claimed unless separately recorded.
Resizing to the minimum window size (900x600) keeps rail, topbar and content usable without overlap or clipping of controls.
Zoom/large text: View zoom in to 150% and 200% (Cmd+=) keeps navigation, headings and settings readable and operable; Cmd+0 restores.

Reduced motion: with macOS Reduce Motion enabled, every automated C01 flow still passes (no control depends on motion), and the stylesheet built into the same native-prepare run contains the shared prefers-reduced-motion clamp.
No Academy learner or gamification element (XP, credits, streak, notifications, earned skins) appears on general screens.
Startup makes no internet connection (referencing evidence/C01/native/startup-network.json for the same executable).

C02.check: Settings > Tenants: the labelled Add tenant form (Label, TSG ID, destination radios, Region pop-up) is operated by keyboard and creates a tenant that appears in the tenant list and becomes the active tenant.

Keychain scan key: the AIRS API key field is a secure text field whose AX value never exposes the key; saving stores one item under the fixture namespace in the dedicated fixture test keychain (item attributes inspected, secret never read) and reports 'Scan key saved in the Keychain.'; the key appears in no AX snapshot.
Persistence across relaunch: after quitting and relaunching, the tenant, its active selection, its Keychain scan-key status and the Dark appearance are restored (C01 carry-over).
Session-only scan key: 'Scan key held for this session only.' with no Keychain item added; after relaunch that tenant reports a missing scan key.

Reviewed endpoint override: Change destination with a custom HTTPS origin shows a review naming both origins and the key removal; confirming changes the destination, removes the scan key (its Keychain item is deleted) and requires a new key.

Profile import through the native open sheet attached to the main window: a synthetic airs-cli registry with an embedded synthetic secret and a credential-file reference previews names, TSG IDs and discarded-field counts, the secret appears nowhere in the AX tree, and importing creates keyless tenants.

Locked credential store: with the fixture keychain locked through the app's own keychain reference (fixture-only menu), saving a scan key reports that the Keychain is locked, shows no OS prompt and falls back to nothing; after unlocking, saving succeeds and the retired record is cleaned up.
Reset local data (two-step confirmation) removes the v2 tenants, preference document and every fixture-namespace Keychain item; v1 Application Support data is unchanged.
Corrupt local data: an unreadable state document is reported ('Local desktop data could not be read'), left byte-identical, creating a tenant is refused, and Reset recovers.

Keyboard and VoiceOver attributes of the tenant UI: Tab reaches the tenant form fields, storage-mode radios and actions in order; per-tenant actions are named ('Make … active', 'Delete …'); a refusal is exposed as an alert.
No internet sockets during startup with tenants and stored scan keys present (C02 makes no scan or validation request).
At 200% zoom and at the minimum window size the scan-key field and its Save action are reachable by Tab and lie inside the window, clear of the bottom fade.

C03.check: Runtime Security is an available destination (no 'Soon'), opens with the heading 'Scan a prompt or response', directs to Settings when no tenant exists, and its scan form is reachable by Tab in order: By name, Profile name or ID, Prompt, Response, Application name (optional), Scan.

Real UI submission through Tauri → Rust → SDK to the synthetic TLS endpoint: the endpoint receives exactly one POST /v1/scan/sync/request (application/json, x-pan-token equal to the synthetic key, x-payload-hash the HMAC-SHA256 of the received body, no Authorization header) carrying the entered profile name, prompt and application name; the window shows 'Blocked' with the verbatim action 'block', category 'malicious' and the reported detectors (including an unrecognized one).

An unrecognized service action, and an allow/benign reply carrying a content-level error while its global timeout and error flags are false, are each shown as 'Not determined' with the explanation that they must not be treated as allowed (the content error listed); 'Allowed' is not shown.
A denied key (HTTP 401) is reported as the tenant not accepting the scan key and as refused (not scanned); the endpoint received exactly one request (no retry).

Cancelling a scan whose reply is delayed shows that the request may already have reached the service (never that it was sent) with no verdict, re-enables Scan, and nothing further reaches the endpoint after the delayed reply time.

Switching the active tenant while a scan's reply is delayed: the other tenant's Runtime view shows none of the first tenant's scans; after the reply time, the first tenant's record says the reply was discarded and shows no verdict; the endpoint received one request.

A lost response (the endpoint closes the connection) is shown as a connection failure with an unknown outcome and the 'send it again only if' guidance; nothing is resent automatically within 6 s; pressing Scan sends exactly one new request.

T23 offline: with the endpoint stopped the app launches and the scan form is editable; a scan reports an unknown outcome that may or may not have reached the service (never claiming it was sent); after the endpoint returns nothing is sent automatically within 6 s; an explicit Scan sends exactly one request and shows its verdict.
Quitting while a scan is in flight and relaunching: the relaunched app shows no scan history and sends nothing to the endpoint within 6 s of launch (no replay).
Keyboard-only scan: the operator tabs to the fields, types the profile and prompt and submits with the keyboard; the verdict is announced through the result's live status region.
Working v1-sized input (a 64 KiB prompt and 32 KiB response, typed as real key events) reaches the endpoint intact (exact character counts, valid payload hash) and shows a verdict.
At 200% zoom and at the minimum window size, the Prompt field and the Scan button are reachable by Tab and lie inside the window clear of the bottom fade.
After the scans, no file in the fixture data root other than the fixture keychain contains the synthetic key or any submitted prompt marker, and no AX snapshot contains the key.

C04.check: Settings shows a labelled 'Academy account' group, separate from Tenants, stating the learner account is independent of AIRS tenants; signed out it offers 'Sign in to Academy', reachable by Tab.

Starting sign-in shows the device code (accessible name 'Sign-in code …') and the issuer's verification page; 'Open sign-in page' hands exactly the issuer-returned HTTPS page to the browser (fixture build: recorded, not launched); the presentation never sends a URL.

After approval in the browser the window shows 'Signed in to Academy as <name>'; the endpoint saw a public-client device flow (client_id, no client secret, no Authorization on identity requests); the learner Keychain namespace holds exactly one item and the scan namespace none; no token appears in the data root or any AX snapshot.
After quit and relaunch the Academy account is still signed in (from the Keychain) under the same name.
Creating and switching AIRS tenants leaves the Academy account signed in under the same name.
Signing out shows 'Not signed in to Academy', empties the learner Keychain namespace and revokes the refresh token at the issuer.
A sign-in declined in the browser shows 'Sign-in was declined in the browser.' with 'Sign in again', and saves nothing.
With the Academy endpoint unreachable, sign-in reports that Academy could not be reached, and nothing is saved.
Cancelling a sign-in that is waiting for approval returns to 'Not signed in to Academy'; a grant issued afterwards does not sign in and nothing is saved.
Keyboard only: Tab reaches 'Sign in to Academy', Space starts sign-in, Tab reaches 'Open sign-in page' and 'Cancel sign-in'; state changes are exposed through a live status region.
At 200% zoom and at the minimum window size, the Academy sign-in control is reachable by Tab and lies inside the window clear of the bottom fade.
Reset local data signs the Academy account out and empties the learner Keychain namespace.

C05.check: Signed out, the Academy destination shows Academy's own catalog ('What will you take up next?') with a note that the learner is browsing as a guest; the endpoint receives only public catalog procedures, none with an Authorization header, and no identity-provider requests.
After signing in, the Academy catalog is read again under the account without the guest note; requests carry the account credential exactly for procedures on the desktop account allowlist.

From the catalog's Courses filter, the course page and its module units open; a lesson exposes its heading and first paragraph and all section headings of a 50 KiB lesson; the trail 'Learn › <course>' links back to the course.

A lesson diagram shows its pre-rendered image ('Lesson diagram') with its source under a disclosure, a diagram without an artifact shows its source, and no diagram video is requested; an external lesson link opens nothing, keeps the window on the lesson and states it was not opened; an in-page anchor stays on the lesson; a learner-path link routes to the catalog in place.

Signed in, a knowledge check starts, takes an answer and submits through the endpoint with the literal fixture request bodies and the account credential; the server's grade ('You scored 100%', '1 of 1 correct') is shown; no answer key appears in any AX snapshot.
As a guest, starting a knowledge check says 'Sign in to take this knowledge check.' and sends nothing to Academy.
A hands-on lab unit is previewed with its title and brief and says no lab sandbox was started; no lab start, step or submit request is made.
Signing out while on a lesson returns the Academy destination to the catalog as a guest with only uncredentialed calls; signing in again reads the catalog under the account.

Navigating Academy → Runtime Security → Harness placeholder shows no learner chrome or effects (XP, trail, reading progress, knowledge check, lab, guest note, probe) outside Academy, and no learner request is made while away.
Keyboard only: Tab reaches the Courses filter and the course link, Return opens the course with focus on its heading, Tab reaches a lesson link, and Return opens the lesson with focus on its heading.
In View > Appearance Dark and Light the lesson text uses the light Gruvbox ink and the dark Paper ink respectively (AX text colors).
At 200% zoom and at the minimum window size, a lesson's 'Complete & continue' control is reachable by Tab and lies inside the window clear of the bottom fade.
Reset local data while signed in signs the learner out, empties the learner Keychain namespace and returns Academy to the guest catalog.

Content access as Academy decides it: a guest at members-only or progression-locked content sees Academy's sign-in gate (endpoint 401, no credential); signed in, locked content shows 'This content is locked' with its progression reason (endpoint 403 FORBIDDEN with the domain code), members-only content opens, and retired content says 'Unit not found.' without any gate.

Failures stay visible and truthful: a guest pressing 'Complete & continue' is asked to sign in, stays on the lesson and sends nothing; a knowledge-check submission the server fails after receiving it says Academy may have recorded it, keeps the answer, hides the server text and is sent once.

C06.check: Signed out, Academy's navigation offers Learn only; signed in it offers Academy's Home, Learn and Program and the web shell's Notifications and Settings. Home shows Academy's own briefing (level and XP from Academy) with no failure toast, and Program shows Academy's hub with its five sections.

The final assessment shows Academy's eligibility facts, starts with the learner's consent and shows Academy's question with Academy's countdown ('Time remaining', counted down to Academy's deadline) and the proctored pill in view; a submission the server fails after receiving shows that submission could not be confirmed, keeps the answer, hides the server's text and is sent exactly once; 'Check submission status' reads Academy's submission state and shows Academy's pending review. No answer key or truth canary appears in any captured AX tree.

Keyboard only: Tab reaches the first answer option, Space selects it, Tab reaches 'See results', Return submits once and the unknown outcome is announced, Tab reaches 'Check submission status' and Return shows Academy's pending review.

The certificate's public verify URL (shared to LinkedIn) is on Academy web's origin, not the app's; 'Download PDF' opens exactly one native print sheet (recorded by the fixture build), stays on the certificate, and makes no learner call beyond the certificate and account reads; when the sheet cannot open, the page says so in an alert region, no sheet is opened and nothing is sent.

A guided lab runs through Academy's desktop attempt contract: one start with the lab id and a request id, draft saves naming the base version with a client mutation id, one grading request naming a confirmed draft version with a submission id, and Academy's pass shown; no web lab runtime call is made. A lab Academy refuses to start for lack of a desktop adapter is previewed with no sandbox started.

In Shift, the unstamped alert is served and the learner's answer is sent and answered (Academy's explanation shown) before a slow optional briefing replies; the answer carries only the learner's choice, and the SLA countdown comes from Academy's stamp.

Removing an enrollment shows Academy's confirmation naming the affected certification and every course it covers and stating that earned certificates stay valid; Cancel sends nothing and confirming sends exactly one enrollment.removeByCourse for the course.

Academy's Settings entry opens the learner account page, which offers 'Change photo' on the desktop and says the app sets theme and accent (no theme choice); its Sign out ends the Academy session through the desktop: the destination returns to guest navigation, Settings shows 'Not signed in to Academy.', the refresh token is revoked and the learner keychain namespace is empty.

Across the run every learner request is on the account allowlist or a public query; no assessor, grading, override, award or admin procedure is requested; no exam, Shift, lab or enrollment input carries a hosted decision (deadline, score, pass, award, verdict or clock); public-only queries carry no Authorization header.
Leaving Academy for Runtime Security and Harness shows none of Academy's learner surfaces (Program, assessment, lab, Shift, removal, level) and makes no learner calls.
On the assessment at 200% zoom and at the minimum window size, Tab reaches 'See results' inside the window and above the bottom fade.

Signed in again (a fresh learner cache) with Academy's deadline seconds away, the resumed assessment's countdown shows it and, at the deadline, the runner submits exactly once and reports the server's unknown outcome; nothing is resent and the countdown stays at 00:00.

'Change photo' takes a photo chosen natively (here larger than Academy's 2 MiB cap), prepares it in the core as a 512-pixel JPEG within the cap, presigns with the account credential (the prepared type and size), stores the bytes at the presigned destination with no credential, confirms with Academy, and reads the photo back from Academy's public avatar address (no credential) so the page shows it without a load warning; an extreme 1x8192 portrait is prepared from its centre and uploaded; a later photo the store keeps under the same address but whose reply is lost is reported as possibly changed (never unchanged), is not confirmed or resent, and the photo at the unchanged address is read again; a file with an image signature that does not decode, and a photo within 8192 pixels a side whose decoded pixels exceed the decoder memory budget, send nothing and says the photo is unchanged; a cancelled pick sends nothing and shows no error; 'Remove photo' removes it with one learner call.

'Reset course progress' asks 'Reset your progress?' with Academy's counts and that earned certificates stay valid; Cancel sends nothing and confirming sends exactly one progress.resetCourse for the course.

A completed lesson asks 'How was this module?' (an unfinished one does not); rating it and submitting thanks the learner and sends exactly one admin.feedback.submit with the module, lesson and rating.

C07.check: Signed in, Academy's navigation offers the desktop's Downloads; the page says what still needs Academy (videos, walkthroughs, live labs); a course is downloaded by keyboard (Tab to 'Download <course>', Return) and listed ready offline with its unit count after exactly one desktop.access and one desktop.bundle, both with the account credential; one offline key item is added to the fixture learner keychain.
Every file under the offline root is a sealed record in a 0700 directory with mode 0600; no lesson text, course id or title, account id or display name appears in any file's bytes or path.

With Academy unreachable, quit and relaunched: still signed in, Academy says it cannot be reached, Downloads lists the course ready offline and offers no download, 'Open' shows the first lesson with its text from the download, and its contents open the second.

Offline, the lab opens from the attempt read while online and an edit says it is saved on this device only; quit and relaunched offline, Downloads names one lab draft saved on this Mac only and the lab reopens with the edit and that status; no request reaches Academy meanwhile.

With Academy back, nothing is sent by itself; 'Save now' sends exactly one draft save on the attempt's base version with a client mutation id and the edit, Academy's confirmation clears the local copy, reconnecting re-checks the download (access and manifest) and shows that a newer version is on Academy, and 'Update' downloads it again.

Signing out removes Downloads (guest navigation offers Learn only); another account sees no downloads and the first account's sealed files are unchanged; the first account signed in again sees its download.

Size and retention limits: a course past Academy's bundle cap (413) is assembled from its manifest and unit bundles each within Academy's 7 MiB cap, and fetching stops as soon as it cannot fit the desktop's 16 MiB record (three of four 6 MiB parts fetched), with 'There is not enough room' and nothing kept; once a download's lease ends its lessons are not read offline and Downloads says offline access ended; a course Academy no longer gives the account says so after relaunch and offers no Open.
'Reset local data' removes the offline root and every learner keychain item, including the offline key.
At 200% zoom and at the minimum window size, Tab reaches 'Download <course>' on Downloads inside the window and clear of the bottom fade.
Every learner request is an allowlisted or public procedure, and every desktop offline procedure carries the account credential.
